clue.text: For mast support a source-of timber? Yes

parts.note: a forest is where timber comes from
AY (aye) is an old word for yes

explanation.surface: A sailor wonders whether a mast should be propped up with wood from a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' is just a link word here. A FORESTAY is a stay (a rope or wire) running from the top of a mast down to the bow.
explanation.definitionFit: A forestay is the rigging wire that braces a ship's foremast from the front.

clue.text: Universal conveyance

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, omnibus means covering everything; as a noun it is the old full name for a bus, a vehicle carrying passengers.

clue.text: Pack up and speak in great detail

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the word for pack is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a bale is a tightly packed bundle
to orate is to speak formally

explanation.surface: Someone is told to gather their things and give a long, detailed speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack up' looks like a phrase meaning 'stop', but 'up' is the reversal signal for a down clue, turning the word for pack (giving ELAB).
explanation.definitionFit: Something elaborate is worked out with lots of intricate parts, the adjective sense.

clue.text: Cashier spill the beans

annotationWithheld.why: Cashier spill the beans (6): 'Cashier' gives TELLER, but 'spill the beans' is a verb meaning TELL, not the noun TELLER; no parse makes the second half define or build the full answer as printed

clue.text: Appearances are deceptive — eventually crone is transformed in play

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are played around with and transformed into a new order

explanation.surface: In a stage play, an old crone finally turns out to be someone else entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is transformed in play' rearranges the letters of EVENTUALLY CRONE. The answer is also the title of a George Bernard Shaw comedy, which the word 'play' hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying warns that what something looks like is no sure guide, the same idea as appearances being deceptive.

clue.text: Something of a volcanic nature, I'm turning purple on the outside

indicators.note: the purple colour word sits on the outside, wrapped around the other piece

parts.note: puce is a dark purplish-brown colour

indicators.note: turning means the letters of I'm are read backwards

explanation.surface: A volcanic rock speaks, saying it is going purple all over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses I'M (giving MI), and 'on the outside' wraps the purple shade around it. Puce is a brownish purple.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumice is a light, porous rock formed from frothy lava.

clue.text: Quiet in the bar, everyone, for a game

indicators.note: the word for quiet goes inside the word for a bar

parts.note: a pub is a bar, a British drinking place
SH is the sound asking for quiet
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Someone calls for silence from everyone in the pub so a game can begin.
explanation.walkthrough: Pushball is a game in which two teams shove a huge ball toward the opposing goal; 'in' puts the hush inside the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushball is a team sport played with a very large ball.

clue.text: I had one of the ears, stupid!

parts.note: I'd is the short form of I had
I is the Roman numeral for one
otic is the medical adjective meaning relating to the ear

explanation.surface: Someone owns up to having had one of the ears and is called stupid for it.
explanation.walkthrough: OTIC is a technical medical word worth knowing for crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiotic is an adjective meaning extremely foolish.

clue.text: Wheels turn before getting to another place

indicators.note: the wheels turn, so their letters are rolled into a new order

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Wheels go round before a traveller reaches a new destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' rearranges WHEELS into ELSEWH; 'getting' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsewhere means in or to some different location.

clue.text: Necessitate putting soldiers in the back row

indicators.note: the soldiers are put inside the turned row
back tells us the word for row is read backwards

parts.note: a line is a row
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve soldiers

explanation.surface: Putting troops in the rear rank becomes a necessity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back row' looks like TAIL, a false trail; 'back' reverses the row (giving ENIL), and 'in' puts the soldiers inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail something is to make it a necessary consequence, so it means require.

clue.text: First stage in my wanderings from the nursery?

definitions.text: First stage in my wanderings from the nursery?

parts.words: First stage in my wanderings from the nursery
parts.note: the nursery rhyme Goosey Goosey Gander asks 'whither shall I wander?', and the first place in the reply is a floor of the house, not a stage of a journey

explanation.surface: A child recalls the first step of an adventure away from the nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'nursery' is a nursery rhyme: Goosey Goosey Gander goes on '... and downstairs, and in my lady's chamber'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the rhyme the goose first wanders to the upper floor of the house, the first place listed.

clue.text: Having gone out only to be different outside

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit outside the word for only
different means the letters of to be are made different by rearranging

parts.note: sole means only

explanation.surface: Someone who has left finds it was only to become a changed person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' turns TO BE into OBTE, and 'outside' puts it around SOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obsolete has gone out of use or fashion.

clue.text: Present, first and foremost in one way

annotationWithheld.why: Present, first and foremost in one way (6): BEST fits 'first and foremost', but no standard reading of 'in one way' gives the remaining OW
annotationWithheld.clue: Present, first and foremost in one way

clue.text: Newton's proposed sacrifice

definitions.meaning: the first name of the scientist Newton
the son Abraham was ordered to sacrifice before an angel stopped him

explanation.definitionFit: Sir Isaac Newton was the physicist; in Genesis Abraham was told to offer his son Isaac as a sacrifice.

clue.text: Concentrated numbers, have concluded

annotationWithheld.why: Concentrated numbers, have concluded (9): TENS (numbers) and I'VE (have) give TENSIVE, but nothing in the clue as held supplies the opening IN; a word looks missing

clue.text: (Peevishly express) complaint

definitions.meaning: to grumble or whine in an irritable way
an ailment, here a pain in the stomach

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to bellyache is to grumble peevishly; as a noun it is a stomach pain, a bodily complaint.

clue.text: Shut out, on the outside, Mr. Ladd; star of "The Bull"

indicators.note: the actor's first name goes on the outside, enclosing the word for shut out

parts.note: Alan Ladd was a Hollywood film actor
to debar is to shut out or exclude

explanation.surface: Actor Alan Ladd was barred from a film called The Bull in which he starred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star' looks like a film star, Ladd himself, but means a real star: Aldebaran is the brightest star in Taurus, the Bull.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldebaran is the bright red star marking the eye of the constellation Taurus.

clue.text: Distressed by any, trace of a chain

indicators.note: distressed means shaken up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is upset by any sign of a chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distressed' rearranges ANY TRACE; 'by' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Catenary describes the curve a hanging chain makes, from the Latin catena, chain.

clue.text: Permitted range of variation in one claret

indicators.note: a variation in the letters means they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wine experts allow some leeway in the quality of one bottle of Bordeaux.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variation in' rearranges ONE CLARET; 'of' is a link word. Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux wine.
explanation.definitionFit: In engineering, tolerance is the allowed deviation from a specified size or value.

clue.text: Making sense, being private in public house

indicators.note: the soldier goes inside the word for pub

parts.note: the local is a British person's nearest, regular pub
a GI is a US private soldier

explanation.surface: Being a private person in a pub is a sensible choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private' looks like the adjective, but it is a soldier, GI.
explanation.definitionFit: Something logical follows reason and is coherent.

clue.text: Love a start to the scale

parts.note: the sol-fa scale starts with the notes do and re

explanation.surface: Someone loves the opening notes of a musical scale.
explanation.walkthrough: In tonic sol-fa the scale runs do, re, mi, fa, so, la, ti.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore someone is to love them deeply.

clue.text: You heard Caruso becoming so harsh-sounding

indicators.note: becoming means the letters turn into something new by rearrangement
the word you, when heard spoken, is the letter U

parts.note: said aloud you is the letter U

explanation.surface: The great tenor Caruso is said to have grown harsh in his singing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' turns YOU into U, and 'becoming' rearranges U with CARUSO; 'so' is a link word. Enrico Caruso was a famous Italian tenor.
explanation.definitionFit: A raucous noise is loud and grating.

clue.text: Bird's eggs turned up on detective's climb

indicators.note: in a down clue the eggs are turned upwards, read from the bottom

parts.note: ova is the Latin plural of ovum, egg

indicators.note: climb tells us the detective's word is read upwards too

parts.note: a tec is a short word for detective

explanation.surface: A bird's eggs turn up beside a detective scaling a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' and 'climb' both reverse in a down clue (giving AVO and CET); 'on' places one after the other, and the 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocet is a wading bird with an upturned bill.

clue.text: Carp mount in the river

indicators.note: the horse sits inside the river

parts.note: the Nile is the river in crosswords
GG, gee-gee, is a child's word for a horse, something to mount

explanation.surface: An angler takes a carp up into the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carp' looks like the fish, but here it is a verb meaning to find fault.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to complain persistently about trivial things.

clue.text: Uniform colour

parts.note: a dark shade worn as the service uniform of a seafaring force

explanation.definitionFit: The dark blue shade takes its name from the uniforms of the Royal Navy.

clue.text: Wax bat here

definitions.meaning: to wax is to grow larger
read as two words, the place a cricket batsman stands, inside the crease

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the crease is the line marking where the batsman stands, so a batter is 'in crease'.
explanation.definitionFit: The moon waxes as it grows larger; in cricket a batsman stands in the crease, the marked line where they bat.

clue.text: Young vehicle attendant shows a lot of bottle

definitions.meaning: a lad looking after a vehicle
a very large bottle holding a great volume

explanation.definitionFit: Split in two, it is a boy who looks after a car; whole, it is a large protective-cased bottle for liquids.

clue.text: Broken leg? You will be cracking up!

definitions.note: cracking up means praising highly; the answer is the praise itself

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone with a broken leg is told they will be in fits of laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' rearranges LEG YOU. 'Cracking up' looks like laughing or falling apart, but means praising, as in 'not all it's cracked up to be'.
explanation.definitionFit: A eulogy is a speech of high praise, typically for someone who has died.

clue.text: Unpunctuality of the former head

parts.note: late means former, as in the late chairman
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: Unpunctuality was a fault of the previous headmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of the' is a link. NESS appears in place names such as Loch Ness's neighbours, meaning a promontory.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateness is the state of not arriving on time.
